description: Restructure the leader's n=256-1024 staging around the profiled generic asynchronous 64x64 pair loader: remove duplicated shape-specific copies, pipeline factor and panel operands through compact shared banks, retain owner-computes publication, and eliminate reloads without introducing padded TMA or global fine-grained queues.

Replaced the fixed-N256 FP32 async tile/pair movers and N512 scalar Numba copies with the profiled generic 64x64 leading-dimension-aware cp.async loaders. This removes 105 lines of duplicate staging while retaining the owner-computes DAG and compact sidecars. Full validation and fresh-input guard passed. Full-grid measured 726.246706 us; affected cells were b64/n256=80.910 us, b16/n512=166.720 us, and b640/n512=1189.537 us.

Extended the generic 64x64 pair loader to independent leading dimensions and used it to co-stage the N1024 factor/panel solve operands into two compact shared banks. Import build and full validation passed, but ranked execution failed when the N256 specialization compiled: the Numba extern declaration still exposed the prior seven-argument signature while the call sites passed both strides. Logged before correcting the declaration.

Corrected the pair-loader extern to accept both leading dimensions. Full validation passed, and ranked execution advanced through N512, but then failed compiling the unrelated grouped N2048 path because the first correction had accidentally added an extra int32 to the adjacent g2048 store declaration. Logged before removing that stray declaration argument.

Re-ran the corrected declarations across the active set. N256 and both N512 ranked cells executed (b64/n256=80.538 us, b16/n512=168.961 us, b640/n512=1171.024 us), but the N1024 batch-60 path hit CUDA illegal-address during the following rank-k launch. The paired loader was issuing its 128-thread 64x64 schedule from all 256 threads in this kernel, overrunning the compact shared banks; logged before adding the producer-thread bound.

Bound the generic pair loader to its 128 producer threads so the 256-thread N1024 panel kernels no longer overrun the compact FP32 banks. Full validation and fresh-input guard passed; all 15 ranked cells completed at 728.906658 us. The paired N1024 solve staging measured b60/n1024=905.153 us; N256=82.936 us, b16/n512=168.155 us, and b640/n512=1175.611 us.

Brief 119 explored generic 64x64 asynchronous staging across N256-N1024. Trial 0 removed 105 duplicate lines and replaced N512 scalar loads; validation passed and full metric was 726.246706 us (N256 80.910, b16/N512 166.720, b640/N512 1189.537). Trials 1-3 exposed and fixed independent-stride declaration and producer-bound issues while extending the pair loader to N1024. Final trial co-staged N1024 factor/panel operands in compact shared banks, passed full validation and all 15 cells at 728.906658 us (b60/N1024 905.153). Best measured branch score was 726.246706 us. Final nsys attempts were issued through the concurrency wrapper but generated no report on this host. Open directions under this objective include splitting the generic loader into 128-thread and 256-thread schedules, pairing N512 update accumulator/operand staging rather than only source pairs, and double-banking N1024 update operands so conversion of the next factor/panel pair overlaps the current MathDx operation.

Continue generic asynchronous staging by double-banking N1024 factor and update operands so conversion of the next pair overlaps current MathDx work. Preserve the corrected independent-stride declarations and 128-producer bound, and measure N256/N512 regressions before extending dispatch.
